dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:3901.text: A round granary. Formed from 禾 inside 囗. A round one is called 囷; a square one, 京.

shuowen:3902.text: An enclosure for raising livestock. Formed from 囗, with 卷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3903.text: A park with enclosing walls. Formed from 囗, with 有 indicating the sound. Another explanation: an enclosure for birds and beasts is 囿.

shuowen:3904.text: A place for planting fruit trees. Formed from 囗, with 袁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3905.text: A place planted with vegetables is 圃. Formed from 囗, with 甫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3906.text: To approach or settle upon. Formed from 囗 and 大.

shuowen:3907.text: To take something from below, draw it in and hide it. Formed from 囗 and 又. Read like 聶.

shuowen:3908.text: A prison. Formed from 囗, with 令 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3909.text: To keep under guard. Formed from 囗, with 吾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3910.text: To confine. Formed from 人 inside 囗.

shuowen:3911.text: Closed on all four sides. Formed from 囗, with 古 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3912.text: To guard or surround. Formed from 囗, with 韋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3913.text: An old dwelling. Formed from 木 inside 囗.

shuowen:3914.text: A privy. Formed from 囗, depicting 豕 inside 囗. A compound of meanings.

shuowen:3915.text: To interpret or mediate. Formed from 囗 and 化. Bird-catchers tether a living bird to lure others; this is called 囮. Read like 譌; also pronounced like 由.

shuowen:3916.text: The number of things. Formed from 貝, with 囗 indicating the sound. All characters in this group are formed from 員.

shuowen:3917.text: The confused multiplicity of things, 紛𧶊. Formed from 員, with 云 indicating the sound. Read like 鄖 in the Spring and Autumn Commentary’s “Huang Yun of Song.”

shuowen:3918.text: A shelled sea creature; on land called 猋, in water 蜬. Pictographic. In antiquity shells served as currency and tortoises as treasures. Under Zhou there were 泉 coins; Qin abolished shells and circulated money. All characters in this group are formed from 貝.

shuowen:3919.text: The sound of shells. Formed from 小 and 貝.

shuowen:3920.text: Wealth. Formed from 貝, with 有 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3921.text: What people treasure. Formed from 貝, with 才 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3922.text: Wealth or goods. Formed from 貝, with 化 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3923.text: Resources. Formed from 貝, with 爲 indicating the sound. Some say this is ancient 貨. Read like 貴.

shuowen:3924.text: Goods or resources. Formed from 貝, with 次 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3925.text: Goods. Formed from 貝, with 萬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3926.text: Rich. Formed from 貝, with 辰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3927.text: Having many abilities. Formed from 貝, with 臤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3928.text: To adorn. Formed from 貝, with 卉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3929.text: To present ritual gifts in mutual celebration. Formed from 貝, with 加 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3930.text: To present the fruits of one’s work. Formed from 貝, with 工 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3931.text: To present or bring into view. Formed from 貝 and 兟.

shuowen:3932.text: A gift at a meeting or parting. Formed from 貝, with 纬 indicating the sound; the precise occasion is uncertain.

shuowen:3933.text: To carry and give. Formed from 貝, with 齊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3934.text: To bestow. Formed from 貝, with 代 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3935.text: To request things from another person. Formed from 貝, with 弋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3936.text: To give. Formed from 貝, with 各 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3937.text: Things increasing one another. Formed from 貝, with 朕 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to send; also, a supplementary addition.

shuowen:3938.text: To send treasured objects as gifts. Formed from 貝, with 曾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3939.text: To transfer and give. Formed from 貝, with 皮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3940.text: To grant. Formed from 貝, with abbreviated 竷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3941.text: To grant. Formed from 貝, with 來 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “I grant you black-millet aromatic wine.”

shuowen:3942.text: To grant rewards for merit. Formed from 貝, with 尚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3943.text: To give. Formed from 貝, with 易 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3944.text: To add things in successive order. Formed from 貝, with 也 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3945.text: A surplus; profit from trade. Formed from 貝, with 𦝠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3946.text: Profit or surplus. Formed from 貝, with 剌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3947.text: To rely upon. Formed from a person guarding 貝, having something to rely on. Another explanation: to receive a loan without repaying it.

shuowen:3948.text: To accumulate. Formed from 貝, with 宁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3949.text: A second or an addition. Formed from 貝, with 弍 indicating the sound; 弍 is ancient-script 二.

shuowen:3950.text: One who is respected. Formed from 貝, with 𡧍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3951.text: To buy on credit. Formed from 貝, with 余 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3952.text: To lend. Formed from 貝, with 丗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3953.text: To pledge goods for money. Formed from 敖 and 貝; 敖 means letting go, while the valuables are to be recovered later.

shuowen:3954.text: To pledge things to one another. Formed from 貝 and 斦. Further explanation is missing.

shuowen:3955.text: To exchange goods. Formed from 貝, with 戼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3956.text: To trade or redeem. Formed from 貝, with 𧸇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3957.text: To expend wealth and resources. Formed from 貝, with 弗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3958.text: To demand. Formed from 貝, with 朿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3959.text: To trade in the market. Formed from 貝, with 襾 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to sit and sell goods.

shuowen:3960.text: An itinerant merchant. Formed from 貝, with abbreviated 商 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3961.text: One who buys cheaply and sells dearly. Formed from 貝, with 反 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3962.text: To buy at market. Formed from 网 and 貝. Mencius says: “He climbed a prominent mound and netted the market’s profits.”

shuowen:3963.text: Low in price. Formed from 貝, with 戔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3964.text: To levy. Formed from 貝, with 武 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3965.text: To covet things. Formed from 貝, with 今 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3966.text: To diminish. Formed from 貝 and 乏.

shuowen:3967.text: Having a small share of wealth. Formed from 貝 and 分; 分 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:3968.text: To hire. Formed from 貝, with 任 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3969.text: To give property in thanks for bending the law. Formed from 貝, with 求 indicating the sound. Another explanation: 戴質, perhaps presenting a pledge; the phrase is uncertain.

shuowen:3970.text: To seek something by offering wealth. Formed from 貝, with 冓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3971.text: Bringing money to consult a diviner is 䝪. Formed from 貝, with 疋 indicating the sound. Read like 所.

shuowen:3972.text: A minor penalty redeemed with money. Formed from 貝, with 此 indicating the sound. Han law: a commoner failing to perform corvée pays twenty-two coins.

shuowen:3973.text: The tribute of the southern Man peoples. Formed from 貝, with 宗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3974.text: To display for sale. Formed from 貝, with 𡍬 indicating the sound; 𡍬 is ancient-script 睦. Read like 育.

shuowen:3975.text: Things not cheap. Formed from 貝, with 臾 indicating the sound; 臾 is ancient-script 蕢.

shuowen:3976.text: A neck ornament. Formed from two 貝.

shuowen:3977.text: To grant. Formed from 貝, with 兄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3978.text: A gift for the dead. Formed from 貝 and 冒; 冒 conveys covering with garments and quilts.

shuowen:3979.text: To gamble at board games. Formed from 貝, with 者 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3980.text: To use goods as a pledge. Formed from 貝, with 占 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3981.text: To present a gift. Formed from 貝, with 台 indicating the sound. The classics also use 詒.

shuowen:3982.text: To buy repeatedly; to mix or interchange. Formed from 貝, with 廉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3983.text: To make a return offering. Formed from 貝, with abbreviated 塞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3984.text: To assist. Formed from 貝, with 尃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3985.text: To supply. Formed from 貝, with 詹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3986.text: A state or settlement. Formed from 囗; under the former kings’ system, higher and lower ranks had larger and smaller settlements, hence 卪. All characters in this group are formed from 邑.

shuowen:3987.text: A state. Formed from 邑, with 丰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3988.text: Under Zhou, the Son of Heaven’s domain was a thousand li square, divided into a hundred counties, each containing four 郡. Thus the Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “An upper grand officer receives a 郡.” Qin first established thirty-six commanderies to supervise their counties. Formed from 邑, with 君 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3989.text: A settlement with an old ancestral temple of a former ruler is 都. Formed from 邑, with 者 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou: the area five hundred li from the capital is 都.

shuowen:3990.text: Five households make a 鄰. Formed from 邑, with 粦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3991.text: A hundred households make a 酇; 酇 means a gathering. Formed from 邑, with 贊 indicating the sound. Nanyang has Zan County, 酇.

shuowen:3992.text: Five 酇 make a 鄙. Formed from 邑, with 啚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3993.text: The area a hundred li from the capital is 郊. Formed from 邑, with 交 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3994.text: A lodging for dependent states. Formed from 邑, with 氐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3995.text: An outer city wall. Formed from 邑, with 孚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3996.text: A relay lodging on the frontier for transmitting documents. Formed from 邑 and 垂; 垂 means border.

shuowen:3997.text: The royal domain’s 甸 and the grand officers’ 稍; 稍 is their revenue settlement. Formed from 邑, with 肖 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “Assign the 𨛍 lands.” These lie within three hundred li of the Son of Heaven.

shuowen:3998.text: Shanshan, 鄯善, a western Hu state. Formed from 邑 and 善; 善 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:3999.text: The state of Yi Yi, a feudal lord in the Xia rulers’ time. Formed from 邑, with abbreviated 窮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4000.text: Zhou enfeoffed the Yellow Emperor’s descendants at 𨜒. Formed from 邑, with 契 indicating the sound. Read like 薊. Shanggu has a county called 𨜒.
